# Avatar Mod API

All avatar functions exposed to scripters via `J.*`.

## Types

All types derive from the base config in `@jamango/content-client`. No duplication.

```ts
// ── Base types (source of truth: content-client/types/avatars.ts) ───────

type CharacterRigId = "big" | "defaultFemale" | "defaultMale" | "gnome" | "imp" | "ogre" | "slender" | "tall" | "wide";

type CharacterSlotId = "head" | "chest" | "waist" | "armLeft" | "armRight" | "handLeft" | "handRight" | "legLeft" | "legRight" | "footLeft" | "footRight";

type MeshSetId = "aero" | "apex" | "aster" | "bubble" | "cloudkid" | "default" | "defaultJumpsuit" | "drift" | "flux" | "frogle" | "gomo1" | "gomo2" | "gomo3" | "gomo4" | "jamAi" | "jestman" | "kiri" | "miko" | "nawt" | "nexo" | "nova" | "pixobot" | "spacy" | "viro" | "yoka";

// Opaque id keyed by MESH_COMPONENTS. Format is `${setId}_${slotKey}_${partName}` for body
// parts and `item_${partName}` for items — but treat as opaque; look up via MESH_COMPONENTS.
type CharacterComponentId = string;

type CharacterAvatarFaceConfig = {
    eyeId: string | null;
    pupilId: string | null;
    mouthId: string | null;
    browId: string | null;
    featureId: string | null;
    eyeXOffset: number;
    eyeYOffset: number;
    zOffset: number;
    eyeScale: number;
    mouthYOffset: number;
    mouthScale: number;
    featureXOffset: number;
    featureYOffset: number;
    featureScale: number;
    browXOffset: number;
    browYOffset: number;
    browScale: number;
    browZRotation: number;
};

type CharacterAvatarComponentConfig = {
    id: CharacterComponentId;
    colors: Record<string, string>;   // "01" = primary, "02" = secondary, "03" = tertiary
};

type CharacterAvatarConfig = {
    rigId: CharacterRigId;
    skinColorPrimary: string | null;
    skinColorSecondary: string | null;
    hairColor: string | null;
    face: CharacterAvatarFaceConfig;
    components: Record<CharacterSlotId, CharacterAvatarComponentConfig[]>;
};

// ── Partial config for additive layering ──────────────────────────────
// Every field optional. Components append per-slot (not replace).

type PartialCharacterAvatarConfig = Partial<Omit<CharacterAvatarConfig, "face" | "components">> & {
    face?: Partial<CharacterAvatarFaceConfig>;
    components?: Partial<Record<CharacterSlotId, CharacterAvatarComponentConfig[]>>;
};

type EntityId = number;
```

### Component IDs

Component IDs follow the pattern `{setId}_{slotId}`:

```
nova_head, nova_chest, nova_armLeft, ...
aero_head, aero_chest, aero_footRight, ...
default_head, default_chest, default_waist, ...
```

25 mesh sets: `aero`, `apex`, `aster`, `bubble`, `cloudkid`, `default`, `defaultJumpsuit`, `drift`, `flux`, `frogle`, `gomo1`–`gomo4`, `jamAi`, `jestman`, `kiri`, `miko`, `nawt`, `nexo`, `nova`, `pixobot`, `spacy`, `viro`, `yoka`.

Not all sets cover all 11 slots (e.g. `gomo2` only has `chest` and `head`).

### Component colors

Each component has a `colors` map with keys `"01"`, `"02"`, `"03"` (primary, secondary, tertiary). These map to material color slots on the mesh. Not all components use all three. Omitted keys fall back to mesh baked-in defaults.

---

## Functions

### Read

#### `getCharacterAvatar(entityId: EntityId) => CharacterAvatarConfig | undefined`

Returns the character's **current** avatar config (after any script modifications), or `undefined` if the entity isn't a character.

```ts
const avatar = J.getCharacterAvatar(playerId);
if (avatar) {
    console.log("Rig:", avatar.rigId);
    console.log("Hair:", avatar.hairColor);
    console.log("Head components:", avatar.components.head.map(c => c.id));
}
```

#### `getPlayerBaseAvatar(entityId: EntityId) => CharacterAvatarConfig | undefined`

Returns the player's **original platform avatar** — the one stored when they joined the server, before any script modifications. Returns `undefined` if the entity isn't a player character.

Use this to reset a player back to their base look:

```ts
const base = J.getPlayerBaseAvatar(playerId);
if (base) J.setCharacterAvatarByConfig(playerId, base);
```

#### `getCharacterPhotoUrl(entityId: EntityId) => string | undefined`

Returns the avatar photo URL for a character entity, or `undefined`.

---

### Write — full replace

#### `setCharacterAvatarById(entityId: EntityId, avatarAssetId: string) => void`

Loads a pre-made avatar asset by ID and sets it as the character's avatar.

```ts
J.setCharacterAvatarById(playerId, J.assets.avatars.DefaultAvatar.id);
```

#### `setCharacterAvatarByConfig(entityId: EntityId, avatarConfig: CharacterAvatarConfig) => void`

Replaces the **entire** avatar config. Use when you have a complete config (e.g. saved snapshot, full reset).

```ts
const saved = J.getCharacterAvatar(playerId); // snapshot

// ... later, restore it
J.setCharacterAvatarByConfig(playerId, saved);
```

---

### Write — additive layering

#### `addCharacterAvatarConfig(entityId: EntityId, config: PartialCharacterAvatarConfig) => void`

Layers a partial config on top of the character's current avatar.

1. **Omitted = untouched.** Fields you don't pass stay as-is, at every level.
2. **Components stack per slot.** `components.chest: [x]` adds `x` alongside what's already there (doesn't replace). Duplicate `id`s per slot are skipped.

Everything else (`rigId`, colors, face fields) simply overwrites when you pass it.

```ts
// Before: chest slot = [default_chest], hairColor = "#abc"
J.addCharacterAvatarConfig(playerId, {
    hairColor: "#000",                              // overwrites hair
    face: { eyeId: "Eye_Editor.png" },              // overwrites just eyeId; other face fields stay
    components: {
        chest: [{ id: "aero_chest", colors: {} }],  // chest slot → [default_chest, aero_chest]
    },
});
```

> Full replace? Use `setCharacterAvatarByConfig`.

---

## Quick reference

| I want to... | Function |
|---|---|
| Read the full avatar | `getCharacterAvatar(entityId)` |
| Get the original platform avatar | `getPlayerBaseAvatar(entityId)` |
| Layer on a costume/modification | `addCharacterAvatarConfig(entityId, partialConfig)` |
| Full avatar replace | `setCharacterAvatarByConfig(entityId, fullConfig)` |
| Reset to original | `setCharacterAvatarByConfig(entityId, getPlayerBaseAvatar(entityId))` |
| Load a preset avatar | `setCharacterAvatarById(entityId, assetId)` |

---

## Examples

### Apply a full outfit

```ts
J.addCharacterAvatarConfig(playerId, {
    components: {
        head: [{ id: "nova_head", colors: {} }],
        chest: [{ id: "nova_chest", colors: {} }],
        armLeft: [{ id: "nova_armLeft", colors: {} }],
        armRight: [{ id: "nova_armRight", colors: {} }],
        legLeft: [{ id: "nova_legLeft", colors: {} }],
        legRight: [{ id: "nova_legRight", colors: {} }],
        footLeft: [{ id: "nova_footLeft", colors: {} }],
        footRight: [{ id: "nova_footRight", colors: {} }],
    },
});
```

### Team colors

```ts
const TEAM_COLORS = { red: "#ff0000", blue: "#0000ff" };

function setTeamColors(playerId: EntityId, team: "red" | "blue") {
    const color = TEAM_COLORS[team];
    J.addCharacterAvatarConfig(playerId, {
        components: {
            chest: [{ id: "nova_chest", colors: { "01": color } }],
            armLeft: [{ id: "nova_armLeft", colors: { "01": color } }],
            armRight: [{ id: "nova_armRight", colors: { "01": color } }],
        },
    });
}
```

### Equipment system (reset + re-layer)

```ts
const equipped = new Set<PartialCharacterAvatarConfig>();

function onChangeEquipment(playerId: EntityId) {
    const base = J.getPlayerBaseAvatar(playerId);
    if (!base) return;

    // Reset to original
    J.setCharacterAvatarByConfig(playerId, base);

    // Re-layer all equipped items
    equipped.forEach(item => J.addCharacterAvatarConfig(playerId, item));
}
```

### Save and restore avatar

```ts
const snapshot = J.getCharacterAvatar(playerId);

// ... modify avatar for a minigame ...

// Restore original
J.setCharacterAvatarByConfig(playerId, snapshot);
```

---

## Design notes

**Why additive layering instead of equip/unequip?** Scripters think in outfits and costumes, not individual mesh slots. A policeman costume = head + chest + legs + skin color, applied in one call. Additive layering makes this natural. Removal is done via reset + re-layer, which is simpler and less error-prone than tracking individual equip/unequip pairs.

**Why per-slot append with dedup (not replace)?** Base components like `default_head` should stay when adding costume pieces on top. If you add `police_head`, both `default_head` and `police_head` exist in the head slot. To start fresh, reset to base first.

**Why a separate `getPlayerBaseAvatar`?** Scripts modify avatars at runtime, but there's no way to get back to the player's original platform look without this. The base avatar is stored at join time and never changes.
